intro: Paragon tiers are for boss events, where Paragons do most of the late damage. They come from the Bloons wiki's boss-event guide and boss strategy pages; costs are Medium difficulty.

paragons.name: Goliath Doomship
paragons.summary: Named among the highest-damage Paragons in the boss-event guide.
paragons.howItWorks: A huge aircraft with frontal guns, missiles and a Carpet Bomb ability.
strategy: The most expensive Paragon, but the strongest and most versatile; with enough micro it works on almost any map.
Micro matters: keep it facing bloons for its frontal attack and over them for its missiles, and time Carpet Bomb.
Maximise its degree: it has the highest boss-damage potential.

synergies.note: Its Carrier Flagship buff.
Power Glove.

worstBosses: Blastapopoulos (meteors cut its DPS and ability uptime)
degreeTips: Most pops come from Flying Fortress, sometimes with Sky Shredder.
Cheapest tiers: 0-2-2 and 0-3-2 for T2/T3, 4-2-0 for T4; 2-0-4 Spectres are the priciest T4.

paragons.name: Magus Perfectus
paragons.summary: Mana-driven damage Paragon combining Archmage, Phoenix and Necromancer; huge burst during Arcane Metamorphosis.
strengths: Very high damage with its big abilities
paragons.howItWorks: Spends mana on Arcane Spikes, a Dark Phoenix and undead bloons, or switches to a Drain Beam to refill mana.
strategy: Let mana fill, then trigger Arcane Metamorphosis for extreme DPS; when mana runs out, use Phoenix Explosion on BADs.
Use Drain Beam on slow bloons; switch it off for bursts.
Master Builder's Power Glove on it is one of the strongest combos in the game.

synergies.note: Power Glove during Metamorphosis.
Submerged, it shortens Arcane Metamorphosis' cooldown.

worstBosses: Blastapopoulos (longer cooldowns, immune to Phoenix Explosion's damage over time)
degreeTips: Cheap T2/T3: 2-0-2 or 3-0-2; cheap T4: 2-0-4 Necromancer; priciest T4: 4-2-0 Arcane Spikes.

paragons.name: Mega Massive Munitions Factory
paragons.summary: Named among the highest-damage Paragons in the boss-event guide.
weaknesses: Short range: poor direct damage against Phayze
Lych can steal Controlled Burst at tier 5
paragons.howItWorks: Lays giant spiked mines that last up to five rounds and split into spike piles, plus a permanent carpet and the Spikeageddon ability.
strategy: One of the strongest Paragons if it can stockpile mines; more placement-dependent than the Doomship.
The best pick for Timed boss events: a stockpile does huge damage fast. Use Set Target to focus mines.
Build it early to stockpile: round 96 for a tier 4 boss, round 117 for tier 5.

synergies.note: Power Glove target.

degreeTips: Flat pierce from degree matters a lot (+1 every 10 degrees).
Aim all Spike Factories at the entrances for pops; cheapest tiers 0-2-2 and 0-2-3, 4-2-0 for the priciest T4.

paragons.name: Nautic Siege Core
paragons.summary: A stall-safe pick that can handle later Phayze and Vortex tiers alone or in pairs.
strengths: Safe when you need to stall
paragons.howItWorks: Surfaced it fires homing rockets at anything other towers can see; submerged it buffs heroes, Subs and other Paragons' cooldowns. Final Strike does massive damage on a long cooldown.
strategy: In late Freeplay keep it submerged for its buffs and faster Paragon ability cooldowns; surface it for heavy boss damage.
Submerge it during Final Strike's countdown: the countdown stops its attacks but not its buffs.
Against bosses, time Final Strike just before the boss arrives (allow for its 3-second arrival delay). Target Last.

synergies.note: Faster Arcane Metamorphosis cooldown.
Buffs heroes while submerged.

bestBosses: Vortex (if kept out of its stun area)
Phayze (with other camo detectors around the map)
degreeTips: High degree is essential unless you only want the cooldown buff.

paragons.name: Master Builder
paragons.summary: Power Glove overclocks other Paragons; Mega Sentries add burst; its nailgun stuns blimps.
weaknesses: Power Glove doesn't stack with Overclock
paragons.howItWorks: Pinning nails that stun bloons, a permanent self-Ultraboost each round, Mega Sentries that detonate, and a Power Glove that overclocks other Paragons.
strategy: Its real value is Power Glove on expensive Paragons: Goliath Doomship, Magus Perfectus and Mega Massive Munitions Factory.
Stands out in Timed and Least Tier boss events; its nails stall blimps.
Power Glove doesn't stack with Overclock.

synergies.note: Power Glove during Arcane Metamorphosis gives some of the highest DPS in the game.
Power Glove target.
Power Glove target.

worstBosses: Blastapopoulos (Mega Sentries can't pop purple; longer cooldowns)
degreeTips: Pair XXXL Trap with Rubber to Gold, Monkey City and Bounty Hunter: income supplies most of its pop requirement.
Overclock and Ultraboost Banana Farms for extra income.

paragons.name: Ascended Shadow
paragons.summary: Recommended against Phayze and Vortex; gives Crucible its camo detection.
weaknesses: Loses its anti-camo bonus if you also use decamo towers
paragons.howItWorks: Three attacks with bonus damage to camo and boss bloons, a chance to blow bloons back, a Grand Saboteur slow and buffs to Ninjas.
strategy: A Freeplay must-have for its slow and Ninja buffs, but don't buy it too early or it steals pops from later Paragons.
Set it to Strong; most of its boss damage comes from its sticky bombs.

synergies.note: Buffs Ninja Monkeys; an all-Ninja defense with Shinobi stacks builds its degree.
Gives the Crucible camo detection.

worstBosses: Blastapopoulos (destroys sticky bombs before they detonate)
degreeTips: Get pops from a Ninja-heavy defense with many Shinobi Tactics.
Cheapest tiers: 2-2-0 and 3-2-0 for T2/T3, 4-2-0 Bloonjitsu for T4; 2-0-4 Sticky Bombs are the priciest T4.

paragons.name: Navarch of the Seas
paragons.summary: Water Paragon recommended against Lych and Phayze; the boss guide plans it around 40 Merchantmen.
weaknesses: Avoid when you need to stall rounds or let other towers get pops
paragons.howItWorks: Six cannon turrets, three fighter planes and ten hooks that reel in blimps; its ability hooks up to two Fortified BADs per round.
strategy: Easy to get to high degree: Trade Empire and Favored Trades income counts toward the pop requirement.
In boss events it's often bought mainly for its buff to the Goliath Doomship.
It shines in Freeplay, but its passive can steal pops other Paragons need, and it doesn't fit stall setups. Target Last.

synergies.note: Its Carrier Flagship buff powers up the Doomship.
Favored Trades fleets build its degree and are buffed by it.

degreeTips: Spam Trade Empire / Favored Trades: their cash counts more than raw pops.
The boss guide saves about $980,000 for a 40-Merchantman Navarch setup.

paragons.name: Herald of Everfrost
paragons.summary: A stall-safe support Paragon that also cools Blastapopoulos.
paragons.howItWorks: Ice lance beams and a snowstorm roar, a strong slowing aura, Super Brittle debuffs, and an ability that can skip boss skull effects and even freeze BADs.
strategy: A cheap support Paragon: its value is the huge bonus damage from debuffs, not its own DPS.
Time its ability carefully: long delay and cooldown, and it can't carry over between rounds.
In Freeplay it complements Bloonjitsu + Shinobi; with Time Stop it's one of the only ways to slow BADs.

synergies.note: Essential support for Ninja Freeplay builds.
Strong synergy with Popseidon and its ability.

bestBosses: Lych (preventing skulls avoids invulnerability and souls)

paragons.name: Apex Plasma Master
paragons.summary: The cheapest Paragon; a good option against tier 3–4 bosses.
weaknesses: Avoid against Elite bosses unless conditions favour it
paragons.howItWorks: Fires volleys of plasma juggernaut balls that split twice and bounce off walls to rehit bloons.
strategy: Its damage depends on bouncing: on wall-heavy maps (Sulfur Springs, Encrypted, Dark Path) it can out-damage pricier Paragons; on open maps it's weak.
Cheap enough for Boss Rush and lower boss tiers; in least-time events sell it after the tier and buy farms.
Low damage per hit and lots of projectiles pair well with debuffs like Cripple MOAB and Super Brittle.

synergies.note: Cripple MOAB amplifies its many small hits.
Super Brittle amplifies its many small hits.

bestBosses: Blastapopoulos (the rocks let it bounce, and it has no ability to debuff)

paragons.name: Crucible of Steel and Flame
paragons.summary: Second-cheapest Paragon; Meteor Impact burst and a Maelstrom flame ring.
weaknesses: Poor against Phayze; Lych steals Maelstrom
Avoid against Elite bosses unless conditions favour it
paragons.howItWorks: Rotating streams of white-hot blades, plus Maelstrom (longer projectiles and a flame ring) and Meteor Impact (big area burst and homing meteors).
strategy: The second-cheapest Paragon; most of its power is in Meteor Impact, so it's very cost-efficient.
Use Maelstrom when the boss is in range; save Meteor Impact for when a boss becomes vulnerable (Vortex shield down, Dreadbloon out of Primary immunity, a few seconds after Blastapopoulos' rocks).

synergies.note: Supplies the camo detection it lacks.

bestBosses: Diamondback (all projectiles hit the head; Maelstrom handles Diamond Bloons)
degreeTips: Put all tier-5 Tack Shooters near the front for pops.
Cheapest tiers: 0-2-2 and 0-2-3, 0-4-2 Blade Maelstrom for T4; 2-0-4 Overdrive if you're transitioning into it.

paragons.name: Glaive Dominus
paragons.summary: Listed for Lych and later Bloonarius tiers; the boss guide doesn't single it out.
paragons.howItWorks: Three boomerang attacks plus an Overcharge ability for a burst of attack speed; strong knockback.
strategy: One of the cheaper Paragons, mainly used against Elite tier 3–4 bosses; not very map-dependent.
In Freeplay it's mostly used for knockback; if it's your main damage, cycle targeting to spread its damage over time.
Avoid using Overcharge near Lych.
bestBosses: Bosses that spawn bloons, such as Dreadbloon and Lych
degreeTips: Degree 40 is usually reached from tiers alone plus a little cash slider; degree 51+ gives full Overcharge uptime.
Cheapest tiers: 0-2-2 and 3-0-2 for T2/T3, 4-0-2 M.O.A.R Glaives for T4; 2-4-0 Turbo Charges are the priciest T4.

paragons.name: Ballistic Obliteration Missile Bunker
paragons.summary: The wiki's boss guides don't recommend it specifically.
weaknesses: Not featured in the boss guides we cite
paragons.howItWorks: Slow, heavy homing missiles that stun and push bloons back and burst into cluster bombs; a passive that can save you from leaking blimps.
strategy: A simpler expensive Paragon: excellent single-target damage, weak against groups of small fast bloons like DDTs.
Pair it with faster Paragons (Glaive Dominus, Magus Perfectus). Set it to Strong (First against Dreadbloon).
Its passive has a long cooldown: treat it as a last resort.

synergies.note: Covers its weakness to groups.
Covers its weakness to groups.
Her totem's life loss speeds its cooldowns.

degreeTips: Higher degree is essential for consistency.

paragons.name: Root of all Nature
paragons.summary: The newest pre-v57 Paragon (v54); not yet covered by the boss guides.
weaknesses: Not featured in the boss guides we cite
paragons.howItWorks: Electrified thorns that ricochet and speed up the longer it fires; a Wrathful mode trades income for huge DPS.
strategy: Watch its Wrathful state: it becomes one of the highest-DPS Paragons but needs lots of cash generation.
Only go Wrathful on tough rounds and when your income is stable afterwards.
Very strong for Timed bosses, especially tier 5; in Boss Rush you can stay Wrathful because skull income continues.

synergies.note: Jungle's Bounty druids ringed by farms supply both income and pops.
0-4-1 Jungle's Bounty farming builds most of its degree.

degreeTips: Pile up pops over many rounds instead of building it as a makeshift Paragon.
Most pops should come from 0-4-1 Jungle's Bounty with a full farm setup.

paragons.name: S.P.I.D.E.R. Monkey
paragons.summary: Sniper Paragon added in v57: bouncing heavy shots with shrapnel, a Cash Drop barrage, an Offensive Supply Drop, an area buff and a charge shot.
weaknesses: Too new to rank: placeholder tier
v57.1 cut its bullets' bonus boss damage from +15,500 to +500 and its shrapnel pierce to 1
paragons.howItWorks: Shoots from a raised platform over the whole map, ignoring line-of-sight; other Snipers can share its target, and Single Out can skip boss skulls.
strategy: An expensive supplement, not a main defense: it devastates single targets (BAD and ZOMG layers) but falls apart against groups.
Life loss speeds it up (Elite Defender): Ezili's Sacrificial Totem gives bursts of attack speed and faster Single Out.

synergies.note: Other Snipers can use its target.
Sacrificial Totem triggers its life-loss speed boost.

bestBosses: Most bosses: bypasses Vortex's shield and Blastapopoulos' rocks, global vision against Vortex and Phayze, stops Diamondback shedding segments
worstBosses: Bloonarius (many skulls make Single Out weak)

basics: Unlock the Paragon with tower XP (500,000–1,000,000) after every other upgrade of that tower.
Have all three tier-5 versions of the tower on the map, then upgrade one of them. Only one of each Paragon can exist; boss events usually cap you at 4.
Degree runs 1–100 and needs 200,000 power for degree 100. Each degree costs more than the last.

powerSources.source: Cash spent on absorbed towers (tier 5s excluded) and the cost slider
powerSources.value: 1 power per (Paragon cost ÷ 20,000) dollars; the slider needs 5% more per power

powerSources.source: Extra tier 5s beyond the three you need
Pops and income of absorbed towers

tips: Aim for multiples of 20: boss damage jumps at degree 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100, so 19 → 20 matters more than 20 → 21.
Several mid-degree Paragons usually beat one maxed Paragon, because each degree costs more than the last.
Spend cash on real towers before the slider; the slider gives slightly less power per dollar.
Farm pops with income towers: XXXL Trap, Rubber to Gold, Monkey City and Bounty Hunter supply most of the damage/income power.
Overclock and Ultraboost your Banana Farms while farming power.
Three Paragon Power Totems equal one extra tier 5.
If you'll sell it later, upgrade the most expensive of the three tier 5s.
Four Paragons at degree 40+ handle nearly every boss, including Elite.
degreeGuide.degree100: At degree 100, damage and pierce double (+10 flat each) and the boss damage multiplier reaches ×2.25 (Normal) / ×4.5 (Elite).
degreeGuide.note: Power values follow the wiki's Paragon page (updated for v57.0). Cash power depends on the Paragon's price on your difficulty, so it's cheapest on Easy. The non-totem sources add up to 255,000, more than the 200,000 degree 100 needs.
degreeGuide.formula: Power for degree D (2–99) = (50D³ + 5025D² + 168324D + 843000) ÷ 600, rounded down; degree 100 needs 200,000.
